newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian bank gains push up stock index.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian bank gains push up stock index.

text.p: Modest gains in banking shares pushed up Jordan's stock exchange index on Wednesday in low trading volume.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.26 points to 156.82 points in turnover of 316,000 dinars ($446,000).
Jordan Gulf Bank perked up after Tuesday's falls, rising 0.01 dinars to 0.86 dinars in trade worth 71,000 dinars, making it Wednesday's busiest stock.

"The price was dragged down on Tuesday because brokers were worried by the large volume of shares coming onto the market," said Nasser al-Amad, head of brokers United Financial Investments. "The bank replied to an AFM enquiry, saying it was financially sound. The reply did help it recover a little."

Blue-chip Arab Bank also rose 2.00 dinars to close at 265 dinars in trade worth 26,000 dinars. But Jordan National Bank, which was relisted last week after merging with Business Bank, fell back 0.04 dinars, continuing a downward trend which has wiped out most of last week's gains.

The gains by Jordan Gulf Bank and the heavily-weighted Arab Bank helped push up the index even though most shares fell on Wednesday. Falling stocks outnumbered gainers by 17 to eight, with another 15 trading but closing unchanged.
Amad said press reports of tension with Iraq had helped to subdue local investor sentiment.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.13 percent to 82.51 points.
